gap: No result ChatGPT cited explains why surge protection stops working on its own: the MOVs wear out with use, and only some strips (Belkin's page lists 'Power Safety Shut Down: Yes' for the PivotPlug BP112230-08) cut power to the outlets when that happens, while others keep powering devices with no protection. Techlicious, an uncited rank-13 result ChatGPT also got, does state this.
standout_why: I compared against HonestFred's 2026 roundup (rank 2/4) and Techlicious's guide (rank 13, uncited). HonestFred only says 'Surge protectors wear out' and that a strip that reports its status beats one that 'silently stops working'. It gives no VPR and never says whether power is cut. Techlicious already covers the mechanism: MOV wear-out, UL 1449 VPR of 330/400/500 V with 400 V or lower advised on all three lines, and shut-off versus an indicator light only. It also names the Belkin BP112230-08 and Tripp Lite TLP1208TELTV as models that shut off. Both cited rivals were out of reach. The Tom's Guide fetch returned only the title. Good Housekeeping blocked the fetch, and the cited UIUC PDF didn't extract. So I can't rule out that they cover this too. ChatGPT's answer says '2,000J+' and 'status indicator' but never mentions VPR or power cut-off. That is a gap in its answer, but not a fact missing from every result it got.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's Belkin PivotPlug pick for a desk or TV that sits out of sight. Belkin's own page lists a 400 V clamping voltage and 'Power Safety Shut Down: Yes', and Techlicious rates it 330/400/400 with auto-shutoff. A spent strip then goes dark instead of quietly passing unprotected power. ChatGPT's 'look for 2,000J+' advice doesn't settle this, because joules don't tell you what happens after the MOVs are used up. For the Anker 2100J, CyberPower and Isobar6Ultra cards, I couldn't confirm from a maker page whether they cut power or only turn off an LED. That remains the open question for those picks.

findings.label: Why surge protection stops working: MOV wear-out
findings.value: "As MOVs redirect excess current away from your devices, they wear out." "Even if a major surge never occurs, small everyday spikes slowly degrade protection."
findings.source_title: How to Pick the Best Surge Protector (2026) - Techlicious
findings.note: Techlicious also says there is no 'meter' for remaining MOV life and that experts advise replacing a strip about every three years.

findings.label: What happens when the MOVs are spent: shut-off vs indicator light
findings.value: "some surge protectors will shut off power entirely to the outlets when the MOVs expire"; "In most situations, shutting off power entirely is a better solution than simply having a light."
findings.source_title: How to Pick the Best Surge Protector (2026) - Techlicious
findings.note: Techlicious warns that an indicator light 'can be easy to miss' when the strip is under a desk or behind a cabinet.

findings.label: UL 1449 Voltage Protection Rating (VPR) guidance
findings.value: Rated in steps including 330 V, 400 V and 500 V; Techlicious advises 400 V or lower on all three lines (L-N, L-G, N-G)
findings.source_title: How to Pick the Best Surge Protector (2026) - Techlicious
findings.note: Quote: "UL refers to this as the Voltage Protection Rating (VPR)."
